clauses.statement: The progress-deadline policy kernel is a pure module with an injected clock, and observe() only extends the no-progress deadline for a progress token that has not been seen before; passing an already-observed token never resets the deadline (heartbeats do not extend life, only monotonic progress does).
clauses.rationale: A liveness heartbeat that extends deadlines lets a stuck process live forever; the original evaluateProgressBounds semantics reject duplicate checkpoint ids and only advance on new checkpoints, and the kernel must preserve exactly that.

story_refs.text_snippet: 同一進捗値を渡してもデッドラインが延長されない（重複進捗の延命拒否）

test_refs.case: duplicate progress values do not extend the no-progress deadline
a NEW progress token extends the no-progress deadline

test_pattern.must_cover: duplicate progress values do not extend the no-progress deadline

clauses.statement: check() returns structured kill causes that preserve the original five codes (max_wall_clock_exceeded, max_attempts_exceeded, max_cost_exceeded, cost_accounting_unavailable, no_progress_deadline_exceeded) with the original precedence order, wall-clock/attempts/cost being independent hard caps that progress cannot extend; classifyTermination distinguishes a policy-sent signal from an external signal.
clauses.rationale: Kill causes must remain auditable in evidence and hard caps must be a final barrier that monotonic progress cannot bypass; external and policy kills must never be conflated because that conflation caused a real misdiagnosis incident.

story_refs.text_snippet: no_progress / hard_cap（wall_clock・cost・attempts別）/ external_signal を区別した構造化causeを返す

max_wall_clock_exceeded is independent of progress and cannot be extended
classifyTermination: a signal the policy did not send is an external kill

test_pattern.must_cover: precedence order: wall clock beats attempts beats cost

clauses.rationale: The kernel extraction must leave one semantic source of truth without breaking the only site that already implemented the full ideal-form semantics.

clauses.statement: A graphify update subprocess whose output stalls past the no-progress deadline, or which exceeds the wall-clock cap, is terminated with SIGTERM then escalated to SIGKILL after a grace period, the structured stop_reason is attached to the thrown error, stdout/stderr accumulation is capped with an explicit truncation marker, and a signal the policy did not send is attributed as an external kill.
clauses.rationale: graphify update previously had no timeout and unbounded stdout accumulation, allowing story diagnose to hang forever with no attributable cause.

story_refs.text_snippet: SIGTERM→猶予→SIGKILL で終了し、stop_reasonが証跡に残る。stdout蓄積に上限がある

wall-clock cap kills the process even while progress keeps arriving
stdout past the output cap is truncated with an explicit marker rather than growing unbounded
a signal the policy did not send is attributed as an external kill, not a policy kill

clauses.statement: The verification runner streams command output, feeds the parsed completed-test count into the kernel as the monotonic progress value so a suite stays alive while tests keep completing and is killed when progress stalls (independently of the wall-clock cap), and an execution killed by a signal the runner did not send is recorded with timed_out=false plus an external_kill_signal attribution instead of the previous false timed_out=true.
clauses.rationale: The previous execFile-based runner could not observe in-flight progress and its `error.killed && signal` heuristic recorded external SIGTERMs as timeouts, which caused a real misdiagnosis incident in evidence records.

story_refs.text_snippet: 外部SIGTERMで殺された実行は timed_out: false かつ external kill として帰属される
